inlines.v: FROL'ICK, adjective Gay; merry; full of levity; dancing, playing or frisking about; full of pranks. The frolick wind that breathes the spring. The gay, the frolick and the loud. [This adjective is seldom used except in poetry. As a noun and a verb, its use is common.] FROL'ICK, noun 1. A wild prank; a flight of levity, or gaiety and mirth. He would be at his frolick once again. 2. A scene of gaiety and mirth, as in dancing or play. [This is a popular use of the word in America.] FROL'ICK, verb intransitive To play wild pranks; to play tricks of levity, mirth and gaiety. The buzzing insects frolick in the air.
